title: Agent-in-the-loop to distill expert knowledge into artificial intelligence models: a survey
authors: Gao, J.; Zhang, Y.; Chen, Y.; Dong, H.; Chen, Y.; Song, S.; Tang, B.; Gu, Y.
tldr: Presents a comprehensive survey of Agent-in-the-Loop Machine Learning (AIL-ML), a framework integrating both humans and large models as agents to distill expert knowledge into AI models, addressing data sparsity and high annotation costs in expert domains.
problem_and_motivation: Large-scale neural networks have revolutionized general knowledge areas but face challenges in expert domains like healthcare due to data sparsity and high annotation expenses. Existing Human-in-the-Loop Machine Learning (HIL-ML) frameworks fail to address how large models can substitute for human tasks, despite their demonstrated capabilities in reasoning and semantic understanding.
approach: Proposed a unified framework called Agent-in-the-Loop Machine Learning (AIL-ML) that integrates both humans and large models as agents in the modeling loop.
Categorized AIL-ML methods into two main phases: data acquisition and processing, and model development and optimization.
Developed formal mathematical descriptions for data collection mechanisms: x_t = f(S_t, D_t, M_t, A_t) where agents contribute to data generation.
Conducted comprehensive literature review of works from top conferences (IJCAI, ACL, KDD, AAAI, NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, ICLR, CHI) from 2018-2024.
Analyzed differences and relationships between HIL-ML, LMIL-ML (Large-Model-in-the-Loop), and AIL-ML frameworks.
findings: AIL-ML framework enables efficient collaboration between humans and large models to construct vertical AI models with lower costs.
Large models can substitute for specific tasks traditionally performed by humans, reducing annotation costs while maintaining quality.
Data collection strategies can be formalized through conditional probability models: x_t = p(x|y, S_t, D_t, M_t, A_t).
Three primary data collection strategies correspond to different stages: before, during, and after model construction.
The framework addresses limitations of existing HIL-ML reviews that fail to explore how large models can participate in the learning loop.
Agent roles have evolved from labor-intensive annotation to strategic tasks like model fine-tuning and output validation.
AIL-ML combines human intuition and expertise with computational power and reasoning ability of large models.

Figure 2: Framework for AIL-ML Methodology → Divides into two main phases: Data Acquisition and Processing, and Model Development and Optimization.

definitions.definition: A unified framework that integrates both humans and large models as agents in the machine learning loop to distill expert knowledge into AI models with lower costs.
A method that incorporates human knowledge into the machine learning process, emphasizing iterative interaction between humans and systems to enhance model accuracy and adaptability.
A framework where large models are integrated into the modeling loop, intervening at stages like data preprocessing or model development to reduce reliance on human annotation.
A technique where knowledge is transferred from a larger, more complex model (teacher) to a smaller, simpler model (student) to achieve comparable performance with reduced computational complexity.
A machine learning approach where the learner selectively queries an oracle (typically human annotator) to label examples that are ambiguous but likely to provide significant insights.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper provides the first comprehensive survey of Agent-in-the-Loop Machine Learning (AIL-ML), a novel framework that unifies human and large model agents in the machine learning loop. The key innovation is recognizing that large models can substitute for certain human tasks while maintaining the benefits of expert knowledge integration. The formal mathematical framework for data collection mechanisms provides a theoretical foundation for future work. The taxonomy of methods across data acquisition/processing and model development/optimization stages offers practical guidance for researchers. The paper addresses a critical gap in existing literature by exploring how large models can participate in HIL-ML, reducing annotation costs while improving model performance.
directly_justifies: AIL-ML framework enables efficient collaboration between humans and large models to construct vertical AI models with lower costs.
Large models can substitute for specific tasks traditionally performed by humans, reducing annotation costs.
Three primary data collection strategies correspond to different stages of model lifecycle.
The framework addresses data sparsity and high annotation expenses in expert domains.
Agent roles have evolved from labor-intensive annotation to strategic tasks like model fine-tuning.
limits: Survey focuses primarily on computer science and HCI conferences, potentially missing domain-specific implementations.
The mathematical framework is theoretical and may require adaptation for specific application contexts.
The paper acknowledges that large models have limitations in expert knowledge domains despite their capabilities.
Rapid evolution of large models may require frequent updates to the framework and taxonomy.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 9.A received high relevance as the paper addresses privacy concerns through human expert monitoring of sensitive data. Domain 10.A received high relevance for its focus on human-agent interaction design. Domain 6.A received medium relevance for predictive modeling applications. Domain 8.A received medium relevance for anomaly detection applications. Other domains were considered but rejected as the paper is a broad survey rather than focused on specific personal finance applications.
